digest.component_or_area: plan-review gate — impact model calibration (plan-v3 → plan-v4)
propositions: divergent_implementation fires on only 7.72% of plan-v3 findings despite being the sole uncalibrated hard-override axis, and is graded `none` in ~90% of the omitted-scope/unenumerated-consumer class (1,173/1,307 findings) it exists to describe

47.7% of plan-v3 findings (8,632/18,085) score all seven impact axes as `none`, yielding impact exactly 0.0, with all seven axes `none` — a population of 770 findings — entirely absent from any override mechanism

the G6 finding fc347224733dccc6b (validity 0.8889, all axes `none`, impact 0.0) should have been caught by divergent_implementation but was not, because the axis uses an ordinal grade set (`none|low|medium|high`) that lacks semantic distinction between plan-text divergence kinds

the three-way symbolic grading (`contradicts_reality` and `omits_required_site` floor at 0.85; `incomplete_enumeration` contributes below 0.60 and never floors) is required to avoid over-firing; an ungraded blunt widening would route 113 findings into the floor (42 runs flipping PASS→BLOCK, 4.3%), mirroring the 2x over-fire from calibration-3's unguarded floor widening

a high-cost LLM-based calibration instrument (purpose-built eval suite or bulk re-review) is rejected in favor of zero-marginal-cost corpus replay and dogfooding, because the gate's already-produced REVIEW_RESULT sidecar corpus (51,964 verified findings; 18,085 on plan-v3) provides sufficient calibration data

the `prod_impact` floor (Fix 2) collides structurally with the novelty convergence floor (`novelty_priority_floor = 0.4`): it lifts findings orthogonal to remediation-loop state, allowing non-terminating recurrence of novel findings across rounds, whereas Fix 1's semantic grading subsumes 26% of Fix 2's value and targets inherently remediable divergence
